definitions: The process or state of paper turning yellow over time, often due to exposure to light, heat, or acidic conditions.
The discoloration of paper, typically from white or off-white to a yellowish hue, caused by chemical degradation of the cellulose fibers or lignin content.
examples: The museum conservator noted the paper yellowing on the ancient manuscript.
To prevent paper yellowing, store documents in acid-free folders.
